arxiv-2301-09167.title: NLOAccess : automated online computations for collider physics Journal: Eur. Phys. J. A
arxiv-2301-09167.creator: Carlo Flore e1,addr1
arxiv-2301-09167.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Carlo Flore e1,addr1. We present NLOAccess , an online platform acting as a virtual access to automated perturbative computations of physical observables related to collider physics within collinear factorisation. We discuss the design of the project and illustrate how, with few steps and without any need of pre-code or code compilation, a user can generate events and calculate cross sections related for instance to quarkonium production and/or heavy-ion collisions at leading and next-to-leading order in α s \alpha_{s} using MadGraph5_aMC@NLO or HELAC-Onia .

arxiv-2307-16486.description: Abstract We use the Kovchegov-Levin equation to resum contributions of large invariant mass diffractive final states to diffractive structure functions in the dipole picture of deep inelastic scattering. pmc-12547269.title: Socio-economic and insurance factors in preventive care: A two-stage weighted structural analysis
pmc-12547269.creator: Florent Nkouaga
pmc-12547269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). pmc-13107466.creator: Si-Hao Fu, Rui-Jing Pang, Yi Yue, Long-Long Xi, Jia Feng, Ren-Rong Liu
pmc-13107466.description: Over the past few decades, atropisomeric biaryl phosphines have emerged as privileged scaffolds in the design of chiral ligands, bioactive molecules, and drug candidates. pmc-13515887.title: Linear and Nonlinear Learning from Spectroelectrochemical Data: Interrogation of PLS and CNN Behavior Under Experimental Scarcity
pmc-13515887.creator: Abderrahman Atifi
pmc-13515887.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spectroelectrochemistry (SEC) provides unique information-rich datasets by coupling molecular spectroscopic fingerprints with electrochemical activity. Despite its richness, direct machine-learning (ML) analysis of SEC data under realistic experimental constraints and scarcity remains unexplored. This work examines how much spectroscopically encoded electrochemical information can be learned from minimal SEC training data in a chemically reversible two-electron redox system, and how model choice interacts with limited experimental diversity across scan rate.
